title.en: Unit 2 Notes — Trigonometric and Tacheometric Survey
title.gu: યુનિટ 2 Notes — Trigonometric અને Tacheometric Survey

h.en: 2.1 Trigonometric surveying — introduction and methods of observation
h.gu: 2.1 Trigonometric surveying — પરિચય અને observation ની methods

body.en:
The idea. Trigonometric (trigonometrical) surveying finds heights and distances from measured angles and one measured length, using triangle geometry instead of climbing the object with a tape. It answers the diploma's everyday questions — how tall is that tower, chimney, hill feature? — from the ground, and it underlies contouring of hilly ground where chaining slopes is miserable.

Methods of observation. Heights come from vertical angles (elevation/depression measured on the vertical circle, Card 2.2); positions from combining those with horizontal distances measured directly (base accessible), indirectly by a second instrument station (base inaccessible), or optically by stadia (Cards 2.3–2.8). Observations are taken face left and face right and repeated; angles to elevated targets also carry an axis-signal correction when the target's marked point is above/below the point sighted. Every trigonometric height, though, begins as the same right triangle: horizontal distance, angle at the instrument, height opposite it.
body.gu:
મૂળ વિચાર: Trigonometric surveying માં height અને distance, માપેલા angle અને એક માપેલી length પરથી triangle geometry વડે મળે છે — object પર ચઢીને tape ફેરવવાની જરૂર નહીં. Tower, chimney કે hill ની height જમીન પરથી જ માપી શકાય છે, અને ઢાળવાળી જમીન પર contouring માટે આ જ આધાર છે.

Observation ની methods: height vertical angle (elevation/depression) પરથી મળે છે; distance કાં તો સીધો માપવામાં આવે છે (base accessible), કાં તો બીજા instrument station પરથી (base inaccessible), અથવા optically stadia થી (Cards 2.3–2.8). Observation બંને face પર અને repeat કરીને લેવાય છે. દરેક trigonometric height એ જ right triangle થી શરૂ થાય છે: horizontal distance, instrument પાસેનો angle, સામેની height.

h.en: 2.2 Elevation of a point — base accessible and base inaccessible
h.gu: 2.2 Point નું elevation — base accessible અને base inaccessible

items.syllabus_item: 2.2 Methods of determining elevation when base of object is accessible or inaccessible

body.en:
Base accessible (Diagram). Tape the horizontal distance D from instrument station to the object's foot, measure the angle of elevation α to the top. The height of the top above the instrument axis is h = D tan α; add the height of the instrument axis above the station, and the station's RL, to get the RL of the top — exactly the bookkeeping of levelling's HI method wearing a tangent.

RL of top = RL of station + height of instrument + D tan(alpha)

Base inaccessible. When a river, building or cliff forbids taping to the foot, occupy two stations A and B a measured distance b apart in the vertical plane of the object, observe elevations α (near station) and β (far station), and solve the two right triangles sharing the unknown height and distance: h = b tan α tan β / (tan α − tan β) — i.e., the distance from the nearer station is b·tan β/(tan α − tan β). If the two stations cannot be kept in line with the object, a horizontal triangle (base line + two horizontal angles) locates the foot first — the general inaccessible method. Worked patterns are in the viva and exam sets; the geometry is identical, only the algebra grows.
body.gu:
Base accessible (Diagram): instrument station થી object ના પાયા સુધીનો horizontal distance D tape થી માપો, top તરફ angle of elevation α માપો. Top ની height instrument axis થી ઉપર h = D tan α; તેમાં instrument ની height અને station નો RL ઉમેરો — top નો RL મળે.

RL of top = RL of station + height of instrument + D tan(alpha)

Base inaccessible: નદી, building કે cliff ને લીધે પાયા સુધી tape ન જાય ત્યારે object ના જ vertical plane માં b અંતરે બે station A અને B લઈ elevation α અને β માપો; બે right triangle solve કરી height મળે છે: h = b tan α tan β/(tan α − tan β). Station object સાથે એક line માં ન રાખી શકાય તો પહેલા horizontal triangle થી પાયાનું સ્થાન નક્કી થાય છે. geometry એ જ છે, ફક્ત algebra વધે છે.

items.syllabus_item: 2.3 Introduction, purpose and principles of tacheometric surveying

body.en:
What it is. Tacheometry (Greek: 'swift measurement') is optical distance measurement: a theodolite whose diaphragm carries two extra stadia hairs reads, on a graduated staff at the distant point, an intercept s that is proportional to the distance. Read three hair readings, one vertical angle, and a point's distance, direction and RL all fall out — no tape leaves the instrument (Diagram).

Purpose. It exists for ground where chaining is slow, inaccurate or impossible: undulating and hilly terrain (this unit's CO: contour surveys of such regions), broken/cultivated land, water crossings, and rapid detail filling for contour plans. Accuracy is modest (about 1 in 1000) but a single tacheometer party fixes hundreds of contour points a day where a chain party would fix dozens. The principle is pure similar triangles: rays through the two stadia hairs diverge at a fixed angle, so the staff length they bracket grows linearly with distance: D = Ks + C (Cards 2.4–2.5 give K and C their values).
body.gu:
શું છે: Tacheometry એટલે optical distance measurement — diaphragm માં બે વધારાના stadia hairs ધરાવતો theodolite દૂરના point પર રાખેલા staff પર intercept s વાંચે છે, અને s distance ના પ્રમાણમાં હોય છે. ત્રણ hair reading અને એક vertical angle લેતાં જ point નો distance, direction અને RL મળી જાય છે — tape instrument થી દૂર જતો જ નથી (Diagram).

હેતુ: જ્યાં chaining ધીમું, અચોક્કસ કે અશક્ય હોય — undulating/hilly terrain (આ unit નો CO: એવા region નો contour survey), તૂટેલી જમીન, water crossing — ત્યાં tacheometry વપરાય છે. Accuracy સાધારણ (લગભગ 1 in 1000) પણ ઝડપ ઘણી વધારે છે. Principle similar triangles નો છે: બે stadia hair માંથી પસાર થતા rays નિશ્ચિત angle એ ફેલાય છે, એટલે staff પર bracket થતી length distance સાથે linearly વધે છે: D = Ks + C.

h.en: 2.4 Theory of stadia tacheometry and the analytic lens
h.gu: 2.4 Stadia tacheometry નો principle અને analytic lens

items.syllabus_item: 2.4 Theory of stadia tacheometry, analytic lens, advantages & disadvantages

body.en:
Deriving D = Ks + C. Let the stadia hairs be separated by interval i on the diaphragm, the objective's focal length be f, and the distance from objective to instrument axis be d. The ray geometry gives distance from the objective = (f/i)·s; measuring from the instrument axis adds (f + d):

D = (f/i) s + (f + d) = K s + C ; K = f/i (multiplying constant, usually 100) ; C = f + d (additive constant, 0.15-0.45 m)

The analytic lens is an extra convex lens fitted between objective and diaphragm that bends the geometry so the stadia rays effectively diverge from the instrument axis itself — making C = 0 exactly and leaving the field formula as D = Ks alone. Advantages: one-term arithmetic in the field (a whole survey's mental load halves), no constant to misremember, errors of a worn C vanish. Disadvantages: the extra glass absorbs light — a dimmer image, poorer in shade, long sights and dusk; slightly costlier optics. Modern tacheometers and total stations (Unit 4) are analytic by design, which is why generations of students still learn K = 100, C = 0 first.
body.gu:
D = Ks + C કેવી રીતે આવે: diaphragm પર stadia hairs વચ્ચેનું અંતર i, objective ની focal length f, objective થી instrument axis સુધીનું અંતર d હોય તો ray geometry થી D = (f/i)·s + (f + d) મળે છે:

D = K s + C ; K = f/i (multiplying constant, સામાન્ય રીતે 100) ; C = f + d (additive constant, 0.15-0.45 m)

Analytic lens એ objective અને diaphragm વચ્ચે મુકાતો વધારાનો convex lens છે જે geometry એવી ગોઠવે છે કે C = 0 થઈ જાય — field formula ફક્ત D = Ks રહે છે. ફાયદા: field માં એક જ term ની ગણતરી, constant યાદ રાખવાની ભૂલ નહીં. ગેરફાયદા: વધારાનો glass પ્રકાશ શોષે છે — image ઝાંખું પડે, લાંબા sight અને સાંજે તકલીફ. આજના બધા instrument analytic જ આવે છે, એટલે K = 100, C = 0 પહેલા શીખવાય છે.

h.en: 2.5 Determining the constants of a tacheometer

items.syllabus_item: 2.5 Methods of determining constants of a tacheometer

body.en:
Why bother. K is nominal 100 and C nominal small, but hair spacing drifts with repair, temperature and age — a contour survey computed with last decade's constants carries a silent scale error. Constants are therefore measured for the actual instrument-and-staff pair before precise work.

Field method (worked fully in Numerical 2.1). On flat ground, peg two (better three or four) points at accurately taped distances D₁, D₂ … (say 50 m and 100 m) from the instrument; read the staff intercepts s₁, s₂ … with the line of sight horizontal. Each gives D = Ks + C; solve the pair (or least-squares the set) simultaneously for K and C. Checks: a third distance must reproduce within a centimetre or two, and the derived K should sit near 100 (95–105): a wild K means mis-taped distances or an unlevel line of sight, not an exotic instrument. Constants belong to the instrument + its optics, so note them on the instrument box and in every field book that uses them.
body.gu:
શા માટે જરૂરી: K nominal 100 અને C નાનો હોય છે, પણ repair, temperature અને ઉંમરથી hair spacing બદલાય છે — જૂના constants વાપરશો તો આખા survey માં છૂપી scale error આવશે. એટલે precise work પહેલા જે-તે instrument + staff જોડીના constants માપવામાં આવે છે.

Field method (Numerical 2.1 માં સંપૂર્ણ ઉદાહરણ): સપાટ જમીન પર instrument થી ચોક્કસ tape કરેલા અંતરે (દા.ત. 50 m અને 100 m) બે-ત્રણ point peg કરો; horizontal line of sight થી staff intercept s₁, s₂ વાંચો. દરેક માટે D = Ks + C લખી બે સમીકરણ ઉકેલતાં K અને C મળે છે. Check: ત્રીજું અંતર એક-બે cm માં મળવું જોઈએ અને K 100 ની આસપાસ (95–105) હોવો જોઈએ. Constants instrument box પર અને field book માં નોંધો.

h.en: 2.6 Methods of tacheometry — the stadia family

body.en:
Three systems, one family. (1) Fixed-hair (stadia) method — the hairs are fixed in the diaphragm; the staff intercept varies with distance; the instrument of Cards 2.3–2.5. It dominates practice because the diaphragm is cheap, sealed and robust. (2) Movable-hair (subtense) method — hairs are driven by micrometer screws until they exactly bracket a fixed staff target separation (usually 2 m); the screw readings then give distance. More precise per sight but slow and mechanically delicate — mostly tacheometric alidades and subtense bars (the horizontal bar version, where a 2 m bar is sighted and the tiny angle measured precisely, reached 1 in 5000+ and was the pre-EDM distance tool). (3) Tangential method — no stadia hairs at all: vertical angles to two vanes a fixed distance apart on the staff; distance from angle difference — slow, obsolete, but examiners still ask it as the no-special-diaphragm fallback.

Choosing. For the diploma field: fixed-hair with vertical staff is the default everywhere (Cards 2.7–2.8 are its two cases); tangential and movable-hair survive as viva vocabulary and as the conceptual bridge to Unit 4's EDM, which replaces the whole triangle with a timed light pulse.
body.gu:
ત્રણ systems, એક family: (1) Fixed-hair (stadia) method — hairs diaphragm માં fixed; distance પ્રમાણે staff intercept બદલાય છે; Cards 2.3–2.5 નો instrument. સસ્તો અને મજબૂત હોવાથી સૌથી વધુ વપરાય છે. (2) Movable-hair (subtense) method — micrometer screw થી hairs ખસેડી staff પરના fixed target (સામાન્ય રીતે 2 m) ને બરાબર bracket કરવામાં આવે છે; વધુ precise પણ ધીમું અને નાજુક. (3) Tangential method — stadia hair જ નહીં: staff પર fixed અંતરે રહેલા બે vane તરફ vertical angle માપી distance કાઢવામાં આવે છે — ધીમું, હવે ફક્ત પરીક્ષા પૂરતું.

પસંદગી: diploma field work માટે fixed-hair + vertical staff જ default છે (Cards 2.7–2.8 તેના બે કેસ છે); બાકીની methods viva માટે અને Unit 4 ના EDM ને સમજવા માટે છે.

h.en: 2.7 Fixed-hair method — horizontal line of sight, staff vertical
h.gu: 2.7 Fixed-hair method — line of sight horizontal, staff vertical હોય ત્યારે

items.syllabus_item: 2.7 Method of fixed hair: line of sight horizontal and staff held vertically

body.en:
The levelling-like case. With the telescope horizontal (vertical circle reading zero/90° verified, bubble centred), read the three hairs on the vertical staff: top and bottom stadia hairs give the intercept s; the central hair gives the staff reading at the axis height, r. Distance is pure Card 2.4:

D = K s + C

and the RL of the staff point comes from treating the central hair as a level sight:

RL of staff point = (RL of instrument station + height of instrument axis) - r = HI - r

Numerical 2.2 works this end-to-end (D = 124.80 m, RL = 99.95 m). Field notes: staff must be truly vertical (staff bubble; a leaning staff inflates s and biases RL — in wind, wave the staff slowly and book the minimum stadia readings); telescope must be truly horizontal, else you are silently in Card 2.8's case with a wrong θ = 0 assumption.
body.gu:
Levelling જેવો case: telescope horizontal રાખી (vertical circle zero check કરી) vertical staff પર ત્રણેય hair વાંચો: ઉપર-નીચેના stadia hair થી intercept s; વચ્ચેના central hair થી axis height પરનો staff reading r મળે છે. Distance:

D = K s + C

અને staff point નો RL level sight ની જેમ:

RL of staff point = HI - r (HI = station RL + height of instrument)

Numerical 2.2 માં આખી ગણતરી છે. Field નોંધ: staff ખરેખર vertical હોવો જોઈએ (નમેલો staff s વધારી દે છે); telescope ખરેખર horizontal હોવું જોઈએ, નહીંતર તમે θ = 0 ધારીને Card 2.8 નો case ખોટો ગણશો.

h.en: 2.8 Fixed-hair method — inclined line of sight, staff vertical
h.gu: 2.8 Fixed-hair method — line of sight inclined, staff vertical હોય ત્યારે

items.syllabus_item: 2.7 Method of fixed hair: line of sight inclined, staff held vertically (angle of elevation & depression)

body.en:
The contouring case. On slopes the telescope tilts by the vertical angle θ (read on the vertical circle) to see the staff at all. The staff, held vertical, is not perpendicular to the sight, so the intercept along the sight is foreshortened: the effective intercept perpendicular to the line of sight is s·cos θ. Hence the inclined distance along the sight, then its components (Diagram):

inclined length L = K s cos(theta) + Chorizontal distance D = L cos(theta) = K s cos^2(theta) + C cos(theta)vertical component V = L sin(theta) = (K s / 2) sin 2(theta) + C sin(theta)

RL bookkeeping. Elevation: RL of staff point = HI + V − r, where r is the central-hair reading. Depression: θ and V change sign together — RL = HI − V − r with V taken positive downward; the safe field habit is to carry the sign of θ through every formula and let the arithmetic speak. Numerical 2.3 (elevation) gives D = 133.27 m, V = 15.18 m, RL = 265.08 m. This card is the whole CO2 machine: from a hill instrument station, hundreds of (D, θ, r) triples become the contour plan — each point located by bearing, placed by D, and levelled by V.
body.gu:
Contouring નો case: ઢાળ પર staff જોવા telescope ને vertical angle θ પર નમાવવો પડે છે. Staff vertical હોવાથી sight ને perpendicular નથી, એટલે sight દિશામાં intercept ટૂંકો દેખાય છે: અસરકારક intercept = s·cos θ. તેથી (Diagram):

inclined length L = K s cos(theta) + C ; D = K s cos^2(theta) + C cos(theta) ; V = (K s/2) sin 2(theta) + C sin(theta)

RL ની ગણતરી: elevation માટે RL = HI + V − r (r = central-hair reading); depression માટે θ અને V બંનેના sign બદલાય છે — θ નો sign દરેક formula માં સાથે લઈ જવો એ સૌથી સલામત ટેવ છે. Numerical 2.3 માં D = 133.27 m, V = 15.18 m, RL = 265.08 m મળે છે. આ જ card આખું CO2 છે: એક hill station પરથી સેંકડો (D, θ, r) ના ત્રિપુટી contour plan બને છે.

title.en: Inclined line of sight, staff vertical
title.gu: Inclined line of sight, staff vertical હોય ત્યારે

title.en: Numerical 2.1 — Constants K and C of a tacheometer (field method)
title.gu: Numerical 2.1 — Tacheometer ના constants K અને C (field method)

body.en:
Given. On flat ground with a horizontal line of sight: at a taped distance of 50.00 m the staff intercept is 0.497 m; at 100.00 m it is 0.997 m. Determine K and C.

Step 1. Write D = Ks + C for both stations.

50.00 = 0.497 K + C ... (i)100.00 = 0.997 K + C ... (ii)

Step 2. Subtract (i) from (ii) to eliminate C.

50.00 = 0.500 K -> K = 100.0

Step 3. Back-substitute in (i).

C = 50.00 - 100 x 0.497 = 50.00 - 49.70 = 0.30 m

Final answer.

╔ K = 100 , C = 0.30 m - a healthy instrument: K is on its nominal 100, C is small but real (no analytic lens) ╗

Validity check. Always verify against a third taped distance before trusting the pair; if K had come out at, say, 112, suspect the taping or a non-horizontal sight before suspecting the optics (Card 2.5).
body.gu:
આપેલ છે: સપાટ જમીન પર horizontal line of sight થી: 50.00 m taped distance પર staff intercept 0.497 m; 100.00 m પર 0.997 m. K અને C શોધો.

Step 1. બંને station માટે D = Ks + C લખો.

50.00 = 0.497 K + C ; 100.00 = 0.997 K + C

Step 2. બાદબાકી કરી C દૂર કરો.

50.00 = 0.500 K -> K = 100.0

Step 3. C શોધો.

C = 50.00 - 49.70 = 0.30 m

અંતિમ જવાબ:

╔ K = 100 , C = 0.30 m — K nominal 100 પર છે, C નાનો પણ ખરો છે (analytic lens નથી) ╗

ચકાસણી: ત્રીજા taped distance સાથે verify કર્યા વગર constants ન અપનાવો; K 100 થી બહુ દૂર આવે તો પહેલા taping કે line of sight check કરો (Card 2.5).

title.en: Numerical 2.2 — Horizontal sight: distance and RL by fixed hair
title.gu: Numerical 2.2 — Horizontal sight: fixed hair થી distance અને RL

body.en:
Given. Tacheometer (K = 100, C = 0.30 m) at station P, RL 100.00 m, height of instrument axis 1.45 m. Horizontal line of sight to a vertical staff: stadia readings give intercept s = 1.245 m; central hair reading r = 1.500 m. Find the distance and the RL of the staff point.

Step 1. Distance from the stadia formula.

D = K s + C = 100 x 1.245 + 0.30 = 124.50 + 0.30 = 124.80 m

Step 2. Height of the instrument axis (the 'HI').

HI = RL of P + height of instrument = 100.00 + 1.45 = 101.45 m

Step 3. The central hair acts like a level sight down to the staff point.

RL of staff point = HI - r = 101.45 - 1.500 = 99.95 m

Final answer.

╔ Staff point is 124.80 m away at RL 99.95 m - one pointing gave plan distance AND level ╗

Validity check. That double yield — distance plus RL from one staff — is the entire economic case for tacheometry in Card 2.3; a chain-and-level party would need two operations and a slope correction to match it.
body.gu:
આપેલ છે: Tacheometer (K = 100, C = 0.30 m) station P પર, RL 100.00 m, instrument axis ની height 1.45 m. Horizontal line of sight થી vertical staff પર intercept s = 1.245 m; central hair reading r = 1.500 m. Distance અને staff point નો RL શોધો.

Step 1. Stadia formula થી distance.

D = 100 x 1.245 + 0.30 = 124.80 m

Step 2. Instrument axis ની height (HI).

HI = 100.00 + 1.45 = 101.45 m

Step 3. Central hair level sight ની જેમ કામ કરે છે.

RL of staff point = HI - r = 101.45 - 1.500 = 99.95 m

અંતિમ જવાબ:

╔ Staff point 124.80 m દૂર, RL 99.95 m — એક જ pointing માં distance અને level બંને ╗

ચકાસણી: એક staff પરથી distance + RL બંને મળે એ જ tacheometry નો આર્થિક ફાયદો છે (Card 2.3); chain + level party ને આ માટે બે operation જોઈએ.

title.en: Numerical 2.3 — Inclined sight (elevation): D, V and RL
title.gu: Numerical 2.3 — Inclined sight (elevation): D, V અને RL

body.en:
Given. Analytic-lens tacheometer (K = 100, C = 0) on a hill station, HI = 251.30 m. Staff held vertical at Q: intercept s = 1.350 m, central hair r = 1.400 m, vertical angle of elevation θ = +6°30′. Find horizontal distance PQ, the vertical component V, and RL of Q.

Step 1. Horizontal distance — the cos²θ law for a vertical staff.

D = K s cos^2(theta) + C cos(theta) = 100 x 1.350 x cos^2(6.5 deg) + 0 = 135 x 0.9872 = 133.27 m

Step 2. Vertical component by the double-angle form.

V = (K s / 2) sin 2(theta) + C sin(theta) = (135/2) x sin(13 deg) = 67.5 x 0.2250 = 15.18 m

Step 3. RL: go up V from the axis, come down the central-hair reading.

RL of Q = HI + V - r = 251.30 + 15.18 - 1.40 = 265.08 m

Final answer.

╔ D = 133.27 m , V = +15.18 m , RL of Q = 265.08 m - repeat at 200 such points and the hill is contoured (CO2) ╗

Validity check. C = 0 (analytic lens) deleted every C term — compare how much longer this gets with C = 0.30 (Card 2.4) and you see why the lens conquered the market. For a depression the same three lines work with θ negative; V then subtracts itself (Card 2.8).
body.gu:
આપેલ છે: Analytic-lens tacheometer (K = 100, C = 0), hill station પર HI = 251.30 m. Q પર vertical staff: intercept s = 1.350 m, central hair r = 1.400 m, angle of elevation θ = +6°30′. Horizontal distance, V અને Q નો RL શોધો.

Step 1. Horizontal distance — vertical staff માટે cos²θ નો નિયમ.

D = 100 x 1.350 x cos^2(6.5 deg) = 133.27 m

Step 2. Vertical component V.

V = (135/2) x sin(13 deg) = 15.18 m

Step 3. RL: axis થી V ઉપર, પછી central-hair reading નીચે.

RL of Q = 251.30 + 15.18 - 1.40 = 265.08 m

અંતિમ જવાબ:

╔ D = 133.27 m , V = +15.18 m , RL of Q = 265.08 m — આવા 200 point લો એટલે hill contour થઈ જાય (CO2) ╗

ચકાસણી: C = 0 (analytic lens) હોવાથી દરેક C term ગાયબ થયો. Depression માં θ negative લેતાં એ જ ત્રણ line ચાલે છે (Card 2.8).

title.en: Formulae, methods and key data — Unit 2
title.gu: Formulae, methods અને key data — યુનિટ 2

body.en:
general: D = K s + C ; K = f/i (aim 100) ; C = f + d (0 with analytic lens)horizontal sight, vertical staff: D = K s + C ; RL = HI - r (N2.2)inclined sight, vertical staff: D = K s cos^2(theta) + C cos(theta) ; V = (Ks/2) sin 2(theta) + C sin(theta) ; RL = HI +/- V - r (N2.3)trigonometric height, base accessible: RL of top = RL of station + hi + D tan(alpha) ; base inaccessible (stations in line): h = b tan(a) tan(B) / (tan(a) - tan(B))

One diagram rules the unit: the intercept the hairs bracket is s on a vertical staff but only s·cos θ across the sight — every formula above is that sentence in algebra.
body.gu:
general: D = K s + C ; K = f/i (aim 100) ; C = f + d (analytic lens સાથે 0)horizontal sight: D = K s + C ; RL = HI - r (Numerical 2.2)inclined sight, vertical staff: D = K s cos^2(theta) + C cos(theta) ; V = (Ks/2) sin 2(theta) + C sin(theta) ; RL = HI +/- V - r (Numerical 2.3)base accessible height: RL of top = RL of station + hi + D tan(alpha) ; base inaccessible: h = b tan(a) tan(B)/(tan(a) - tan(B))

આખું unit એક વાક્યમાં: vertical staff પર intercept s છે, પણ sight ને કાટખૂણે તે s·cos θ જ ગણાય — બધા formula એ જ વાતનું algebra છે.

name.en: Key data — accuracy, limits and field checks
name.gu: Key data — accuracy, મર્યાદા અને field checks

body.en:
tacheometric accuracy approx 1 in 1000 (vs 1 in 5000 plus for careful taping) - detail/contour work, never boundary controlstaff must be vertical: lean of the staff inflates s and falsifies RL ; wave the staff and book the minimum stadia readingsconstants: determine on taped bases (50/100 m), verify on a third ; K outside 95-105 means field blunder first, optics second (N2.1)observe vertical angles on both faces ; depressions carry theta negative through D, V and RL alike

Speed is the method's virtue and its temptation: tacheometry trades the tape's precision for a contour plan finished today.
body.gu:
tacheometry ની accuracy આશરે 1 in 1000 — detail/contour work માટે, boundary control માટે ક્યારેય નહીંstaff vertical જ હોવો જોઈએ: નમેલો staff s વધારે છે અને RL ખોટો આપે છે; staff ધીમે હલાવી minimum stadia reading નોંધોconstants taped base (50/100 m) પર શોધો, ત્રીજા distance થી verify કરો; K 95-105 ની બહાર એટલે પહેલા field ભૂલ, પછી optics (Numerical 2.1)vertical angle બંને face પર લો; depression માં theta negative દરેક formula માં સાથે લઈ જાઓ

ઝડપ આ method નો ગુણ છે અને લાલચ પણ: tacheometry tape ની precision ના બદલામાં આજે પૂરો થતો contour plan આપે છે.

q.en: Tacheometry in one sentence — principle included.
q.gu: Tacheometry એક વાક્યમાં — principle સાથે.

a.en: Optical distance measurement by similar triangles: two fixed stadia hairs bracket an intercept s on a staff, and distance follows as D = Ks + C (K = f/i ≈ 100), with the vertical angle simultaneously delivering the point's RL.
a.gu: Similar triangles થી optical distance measurement: બે fixed stadia hairs staff પર intercept s બાંધે છે, અને distance D = Ks + C (K = f/i ≈ 100) મળે છે; vertical angle સાથે point નો RL પણ સાથે મળે છે.

q.en: Where does C = f + d actually live in the instrument?
q.gu: C = f + d ખરેખર instrument માં ક્યાં રહે છે?

a.en: f is the objective's focal length — the stadia geometry is anchored at the objective — and d is the small distance from objective to the trunnion/instrument axis from which distances are reckoned. The analytic lens re-anchors the geometry at the axis, so C vanishes.
a.gu: f એ objective ની focal length છે — stadia geometry objective પાસેથી શરૂ થાય છે — અને d એ objective થી instrument axis સુધીનું નાનું અંતર છે. Analytic lens geometry ને axis પર લાવી દે છે, એટલે C = 0 થઈ જાય છે.

q.en: Why is the additive constant the first casualty of good design?
q.gu: સારી design માં additive constant પહેલા કેમ દૂર થાય છે?

a.en: Because C taxes every single observation with an extra term to add (and to get wrong), while contributing nothing to accuracy; making it zero by an analytic lens halves field arithmetic — Numerical 2.3 shows the saving line by line.
a.gu: કારણ કે C દરેક observation માં વધારાનો term ઉમેરે છે (અને ભૂલની તક પણ), જ્યારે accuracy માં કંઈ આપતો નથી; analytic lens થી C = 0 થતાં field ગણતરી અડધી થઈ જાય છે — Numerical 2.3 જુઓ.

q.en: A leaning staff: what breaks, distance or level?
q.gu: નમેલો staff: શું બગડે — distance કે level?

a.en: Both. Lean away/towards tilts the intercepted length (s reads wrong, so D errs); lean sideways barely affects s but the central-hair reading r is taken at the wrong height — RL errs. Hence the staff bubble and 'wave the staff, book the minimum'.
a.gu: બંને. આગળ-પાછળ નમે તો intercept s ખોટો વંચાય (D ખોટો); બાજુમાં નમે તો central hair reading r ખોટી height પર લેવાય (RL ખોટો). એટલે staff bubble અને 'staff હલાવી minimum reading નોંધો' એ નિયમ છે.

q.en: In the inclined-sight formula, why cos²θ and not cos θ?
q.gu: Inclined-sight formula માં cos θ નહીં, cos²θ કેમ?

a.en: One cos θ converts the vertical-staff intercept into the intercept perpendicular to the sight (the true stadia geometry); the second cos θ resolves the resulting inclined length into horizontal distance. Two geometric taxes, two cosines (Card 2.8).
a.gu: એક cos θ vertical staff ના intercept ને sight ને perpendicular intercept માં ફેરવે છે; બીજો cos θ inclined length ને horizontal distance માં ફેરવે છે. બે geometry કર, બે cosine (Card 2.8).

q.en: Your derived constants come out K = 118, C = 0.1. Next action?
q.gu: Constants K = 118, C = 0.1 મળ્યા. આગળનું પગલું?

a.en: Distrust the field work, not the catalogue: re-tape the base distances, verify the sight was truly horizontal, re-read intercepts — K outside 95–105 almost always means blundered bases. Only a clean repeat earns new constants (Numerical 2.1).
a.gu: Catalogue પર નહીં, field work પર શંકા કરો: base distance ફરી tape કરો, sight horizontal હતી તે check કરો, intercept ફરી વાંચો — K 95–105 ની બહાર એટલે લગભગ હંમેશા field ભૂલ. સ્વચ્છ repeat પછી જ નવા constants (Numerical 2.1).

q.en: Base of a chimney is across a river. Height procedure in four steps?
q.gu: Chimney નો પાયો નદીની પેલે પાર છે. Height ની રીત ચાર step માં?

a.en: Lay a measured base line b in line with the chimney on your bank; observe angle of elevation to the top from both ends (α near, β far); solve the shared-height triangles h = b·tan α·tan β/(tan α − tan β); add instrument height and station RL (Card 2.2).
a.gu: તમારા કિનારે chimney ની line માં measured base line b લો; બંને છેડેથી top તરફ angle of elevation (α પાસે, β દૂર) માપો; h = b·tan α·tan β/(tan α − tan β) ઉકેલો; instrument height અને station RL ઉમેરો (Card 2.2).

q.en: Fixed hair versus movable hair — the examinable difference?
q.gu: Fixed hair vs movable hair — પરીક્ષાનો તફાવત?

a.en: Fixed hair: diaphragm interval i fixed, staff intercept s varies, D = Ks + C. Movable (subtense): staff targets fixed (2 m apart), hair interval driven by micrometer until it matches — distance from screw travel. Same triangles, inverted variables.
a.gu: Fixed hair: diaphragm interval i fixed, staff intercept s બદલાય, D = Ks + C. Movable (subtense): staff targets fixed (2 m અંતરે), hair interval micrometer થી ખસેડી match કરવામાં આવે છે. Triangle એ જ, variable ઊલટા.

q.en: Why does CO2 pair the tacheometer with hilly contours specifically?
q.gu: CO2 માં tacheometer ખાસ hilly contour સાથે કેમ જોડાયું છે?

a.en: Because on slopes the alternatives collapse: chaining needs slope corrections on every length and levelling climbs bench by bench, while one inclined tacheometric sight already returns D and V — distance and height together, exactly what a contour point is (Numerical 2.3).
a.gu: કારણ કે ઢાળ પર વિકલ્પો તૂટી પડે છે: chaining માં દરેક length પર slope correction અને levelling પગથિયા-દર-પગથિયા ચઢે છે, જ્યારે એક inclined tacheometric sight D અને V બંને આપે છે — distance + height, એટલે કે contour point (Numerical 2.3).

q.en: Angle of depression case: which signs do you actually change in the book?
q.gu: Angle of depression માં book માં ક્યા sign બદલશો?

a.en: Only θ's: enter θ negative and let D = Ks cos²θ (unchanged — cos² is sign-blind), V = (Ks/2) sin 2θ (comes out negative), RL = HI + V − r (drops correctly). Carrying the sign beats rewriting formulas (Card 2.8).
a.gu: ફક્ત θ નો: θ negative નોંધો — D = Ks cos²θ એમ જ રહે (cos² sign જોતું નથી), V = (Ks/2) sin 2θ negative આવે, RL = HI + V − r બરાબર નીચે આવે. Formula ફરી લખવા કરતાં sign સાથે લઈ જવો સારો (Card 2.8).

q.en: What limits a stadia sight's length in practice?
q.gu: Stadia sight ની length વ્યવહારમાં શું મર્યાદિત કરે છે?

a.en: Reading the intercept: beyond ~150–200 m the hair spacing on the staff blurs (heat shimmer, staff graduation size), and a 1 mm misread of s is 0.1 m of distance at K = 100. Contour parties keep sights short and numerous.
a.gu: Intercept વાંચવાની ક્ષમતા: 150–200 m પછી hair અંતર ઝાંખું પડે છે (ગરમીની ઝાકળ, staff graduation); s માં 1 mm ભૂલ = K = 100 પર 0.1 m distance ભૂલ. એટલે sight ટૂંકા અને ઘણા રાખવામાં આવે છે.

q.en: Trigonometric heighting versus ordinary levelling for a tower top — when is each honest?
q.gu: Tower top માટે trigonometric heighting vs levelling — ક્યારે કયું પ્રામાણિક?

a.en: Levelling cannot reach a tower top at all (no staff station up there) — trigonometric heighting is the only ground method; for reachable points, levelling wins on precision (millimetres vs decimetres). Method follows accessibility first, accuracy second.
a.gu: Levelling tower top સુધી પહોંચી જ નથી શકતું (ત્યાં staff ઊભો ન રહે) — trigonometric heighting જ એક જમીન પરની રીત છે; પહોંચાય એવા point માટે levelling વધુ precise (mm vs dm). રીત પહેલા accessibility, પછી accuracy પ્રમાણે પસંદ થાય છે.

q.en: Define tacheometry. Derive the stadia formula D = Ks + C, defining K and C, and explain how an analytic lens makes C zero, with its advantages and disadvantages.
q.gu: Tacheometry ની વ્યાખ્યા આપો. Stadia formula D = Ks + C તારવો (K અને C સમજાવીને), અને analytic lens C ને zero કેવી રીતે કરે છે તે તેના ફાયદા-ગેરફાયદા સાથે સમજાવો.

q.en: Describe the field method of determining the multiplying and additive constants of a tacheometer, with a worked pair of observations (50 m and 100 m bases).
q.gu: Tacheometer ના multiplying અને additive constants શોધવાની field method વર્ણવો, 50 m અને 100 m base ના observation ના ઉદાહરણ સાથે.

q.en: Explain the fixed-hair method when (a) the line of sight is horizontal and (b) inclined with the staff held vertical, deriving D and V for the inclined case (angle of elevation).
q.gu: Fixed-hair method સમજાવો જ્યારે (a) line of sight horizontal હોય અને (b) staff vertical સાથે inclined હોય; inclined case (angle of elevation) માટે D અને V ના formula તારવો.

q.en: A tower's base is inaccessible across a river. Describe the two-station method (stations in line with the object) to find its height, with the formula derived from the two triangles.
q.gu: Tower નો પાયો નદી પાર inaccessible છે. તેની height શોધવાની two-station method (station object ની line માં) બે triangle પરથી formula તારવીને વર્ણવો.

q.en: Compare fixed-hair, movable-hair (subtense) and tangential methods of tacheometry, stating where each is used.
q.gu: Tacheometry ની fixed-hair, movable-hair (subtense) અને tangential methods ની સરખામણી કરો, દરેક ક્યાં વપરાય છે તે સાથે.

q.en: State the purpose of tacheometric surveying and why it is preferred for contour surveys of hilly/undulating regions (CO2). What accuracy is expected?
q.gu: Tacheometric surveying નો હેતુ જણાવો અને hilly/undulating region ના contour survey માટે તે શા માટે પસંદગીય છે તે સમજાવો (CO2). કેટલી accuracy અપેક્ષિત છે?

q.en: (a) With K = 100, C = 0.30 m, s = 1.245 m on a horizontal sight and central hair 1.500 m, the HI being 101.45 m — find distance and RL of the staff point. (b) For an analytic tacheometer (C = 0), s = 1.350 m at +6°30′ elevation, HI = 251.30 m, r = 1.400 m — find D, V and RL.
q.gu: (a) K = 100, C = 0.30 m, horizontal sight પર s = 1.245 m, central hair 1.500 m, HI = 101.45 m — distance અને staff point નો RL શોધો. (b) Analytic tacheometer (C = 0) માટે s = 1.350 m, elevation +6°30′, HI = 251.30 m, r = 1.400 m — D, V અને RL શોધો.

q.en: A theodolite at station A (RL 150.00 m, instrument height 1.45 m) observes the top of a chimney at an angle of elevation 18°20′; horizontal distance taped 85.0 m (base accessible). Find the RL of the chimney top. Also state the stadia observation checks (staff verticality, both faces) you would apply in the field.
q.gu: Station A (RL 150.00 m, instrument height 1.45 m) પરથી chimney ના top તરફ angle of elevation 18°20′; base accessible હોવાથી taped horizontal distance 85.0 m. Chimney top નો RL શોધો. Field માં લાગુ પડતા stadia checks (staff verticality, બંને face) પણ જણાવો.
